title: How do we know a tile design is symmetric?
description: Four coloured tiles are laid in a block of two tiles by two tiles, twice. The first design is made with mirror pictures and passes the fold test. The second design is made with a half turn, passes the turn test, and has no fold line at all.
teaching_notes: One idea: a design is symmetric if either the fold test or the turn test passes. Watch for students who think a design with no line of symmetry has no symmetry at all.

video_script.why: The child makes two symmetric designs from tiles, one by mirror pictures and one by a half turn, and learns that either a fold or a turn is enough to show symmetry.
video_script.substitution: The book's own coloured tiles, laid in a block of two tiles by two tiles, as one example of an open design.
video_script.anchor: the book's coloured tiles, each a square cut by a slanting line into a blue triangle and a yellow triangle, laid in a block of two tiles by two tiles
video_script.payoff_line: A design is symmetric when its fold test or its turn test passes

final_answer.value: open ended: any design with a line of symmetry or an angle of symmetry, such as the two designs made here
final_answer.spoken: the answer is open ended, and any design with a line of symmetry or an angle of symmetry is correct, such as the two designs made here

hold_back: any design with a line of symmetry or an angle of symmetry
never_show: a design with neither a fold line nor a turn shown as symmetric
a mirror picture drawn without flipping the tiles
maths_rules: the question is open ended; the blocks of 2 tiles by 2 tiles are one example
tile code: the corner where the blue triangle has its right angle: TL top left, TR top right, BL bottom left, BR bottom right
mirror across the vertical line swaps TL with TR and BL with BR; mirror across the horizontal line swaps TL with BL and TR with BR; a half turn swaps TL with BR and TR with BL

design one, rows from the top: TL TR / BL BR (a tile TL in the top left, flipped across the vertical line, then the top row flipped across the line from side to side); the vertical fold and the fold from side to side both match
design two, rows from the top: TL TL / BR BR (the top row TL TL turned halfway round about the centre gives BR BR); a half turn fits

design two: the vertical fold would need TR beside TL but it has TL; the fold from side to side would need BL under TL but it has BR; both slanting folds also fail; so design two has no line of symmetry but has an angle of symmetry
slip: no line of symmetry does not mean no symmetry; the turn test can pass when the fold test fails
video_script.design: One idea: either test is enough, the fold test or the turn test. Two blocks of two by two tiles, built one after the other. Flip arrows are teal, the turn arrow is amber and the centre dot is red.

narration: <bookmark mark='line'/>A fold line where both halves cover each other is called a line of symmetry.
<bookmark mark='angle'/>A turn about the centre that makes the design look the same is called an angle of symmetry.
<bookmark mark='block'/>We build each design in a block of two tiles by two tiles.
